actions.description: Share what you have verified — a damage figure, a case count, a claim decision, a deadline — with every other team. Free and always available; the cheapest way to keep two agencies from working off two different numbers.

Teams go out and count what was lost in the area you name — homes, businesses, public systems, income — with photographs and costs. Gives a documented figure that programs can be decided on; it counts only what the teams reached and what people were willing to show them.

The state asks the federal government, in writing, for an emergency or major disaster declaration for the counties you name, with the damage on record. Without a request nothing federal opens; a request is a case, and it is only as strong as the documentation behind it.

Open one federal program for the declared counties — public assistance for government repairs, or individual assistance for households. Money starts to move; each program has its own eligibility rules, and the people they leave out stay out.

available_to: Virginia Department of Housing and Community Development
actions.description: Commit state or regional money to cover the local share of a federal program for the places you name. Lets counties that cannot pay their share take part; the money is not spent on anything else.

Apply for federal mitigation money for one project that makes the next failure smaller — a second route, a hardened site, a backup system. Funds the version that would have held; the money takes months to arrive and the project years to finish.

available_to: Virginia Department of Housing and Community Development
actions.description: Staff and volunteers help households in one area register for assistance and assemble the documents it asks for. More eligible people apply; the program's rules do not change because they did.

available_to: Virginia Department of Housing and Community Development
actions.description: Accept other proof of ownership or occupancy — a tax receipt, a utility bill, a signed statement from neighbours — for one program. Opens aid to heirs' property families and informal renters; some of what is accepted will be wrong.

available_to: SBA Office of Disaster Recovery and Resilience
actions.description: Offer low-interest disaster loans to businesses and households in the declared area. Puts capital in reach quickly; it is debt, and the businesses hit hardest are the ones least able to take more.

available_to: Virginia Department of Housing and Community Development
SBA Office of Disaster Recovery and Resilience
actions.description: Grant money that does not have to be repaid, for one group you name — small businesses, workers, households. Keeps them going until slower money arrives; there is never enough for everyone who applies.

available_to: SBA Office of Disaster Recovery and Resilience
actions.description: Open a walk-in center where businesses get help with loans, grants, insurance claims and lost records. Turns programs into applications; it serves the people who come through the door.

available_to: Virginia Department of Housing and Community Development
actions.description: Repair or replace the damaged parts of homes in one area — plumbing, wells, heating. Makes homes livable; contractors are scarce and every job takes longer than promised.

available_to: Virginia Department of Housing and Community Development
actions.description: Pay a set number of months of back rent or mortgage for eligible households. Stops evictions for those months; does nothing about the income that was lost.

available_to: Virginia Department of Housing and Community Development
actions.description: Assign case managers to households with open needs, each working through what programs exist and what is still unmet. The only way the hardest cases get finished; each manager can carry only so many.
Organise volunteer crews from churches and national groups for repair work in one area. Cheap labour for simple jobs; volunteers come for weeks, not years, and cannot do licensed work.

An administrative letter to every insurer licensed in Virginia setting out how claims from this event must be handled and explained. Insurers must follow it; it cannot rewrite a policy that excludes the loss.
Examine one insurer's handling of claims from this event, with powers to require records and order corrections. Finds and fixes improper denials; takes months and makes an adversary of the company.

available_to: SBA Office of Disaster Recovery and Resilience
actions.description: Volunteer lawyers and adjusters help policyholders file, document and appeal claims. More claims get paid that should be paid; it only helps people who come and who had insurance.
Restore a damaged system exactly as it was. Fastest and cheapest way back; it can fail the same way again.
Rebuild a system with a second path, a backup site or a manual fallback, so a single failure cannot take it down. The version that would have held; it costs more and takes months longer.
Equip clinics, libraries and homes in one area for remote visits. Brings specialists to people who cannot travel; it depends on a connection that was the thing the attack cut.

Keep a service opened during the crisis — chairs, a clinic, a staffed site — running permanently, with its staff and budget. People keep the care they came to rely on; the money comes out of something else every year.

Enrol people exposed during the crisis in a registry with follow-up screening for years. Finds the illness that appears late, and records who was exposed; enrolment depends on people trusting who runs it.
Fund a cohort of workers through a training program for jobs that exist in the region. Gives people a path to stay; the jobs at the end have to be there too.
Offer loan repayment, stipends or guaranteed positions to people who commit to staying and working in the region. Keeps some who would have left; buys a commitment of years, not a career.
Fund reclamation of one abandoned or forfeited mine site, hiring local crews. Treats the water and the land, and puts miners to work for the life of the project.
Revoke an operator's permit and call in its reclamation bond, or order it to post more. Secures what the bond covers; often much less than the cleanup costs, and the company may contest it in court.
Write and adopt the recovery plan for the area: what is rebuilt, in what order, with what money. The plan grant programs read; it is only as fair as the process that wrote it.

Hold meetings in the places you name — churches, fire halls, schools — with transport and childcare, and record what people ask for. Hears from people who do not come to county offices; they want to see what is done with what they said.
Publish an account of what failed, who decided what, and what will change, with names and dates. The record the region learns from; somebody comes out of it badly.
